    cfg.fig_route_map()

    cfg.fig_demand_vs_capacity()

    These figures show departing and arriving totals for seats on all carriers and total average demand for all markets.

    Points are colored by the airport’s path flow share. This is computed by taking an enumeration of all paths that utilize each airport, and finding the fraction of all those paths where this airport is a connection rather than the path origin or destination. We expect hubs to have relatively high path flow shares, focus cities (if any carriers are not operating a strict hub-and-spoke system) to have lower values, and spokes to have low or zero path flow shares.

    A red diagonal 1:1 reference line is also included in each panel. If the network is well calibrated the spoke airports should have marks close to or slightly below the red line, while hub airports can be well above the line (i.e. local passengers at that airport need not be available in sufficient quantity to fill planes at that airport).

    cfg.fig_duration_by_distance()

    This figure shows the distance compared against the block time for each leg. It is useful to catch encoding problems for the network schedule, which might have impacts on customer choice behaviour (i.e. if one leg is unusually fast or slow compared to others in the same market.). Each leg is marked with a wedge showing the average bearing for the great circle routing. In this network we can see a reasonable setup where eastbound legs tend to have slightly higher speeds and shorter block times.

    cfg.fig_reference_price_by_distance()

    cfg.fig_booking_curves()

    We can use a schedule viewer to review the schedule at any airport, although reviewing the hub airports will be most useful. Clicking on any leg in these figures will highlight all available connections at this airport that use that leg.

    import pandas as pd

    def check_market_windows(cfg):
    legs_df = cfg.dataframes.legs
    earliest_dep = {}
    latest_dep = {}
    earliest_arr = {}
    latest_arr = {}
    for p in cfg.paths:
        mkt = p.market_identifier
        deptime = legs_df.loc[p.legs[0]].dep_time
        arrtime = legs_df.loc[p.legs[-1]].arr_time
        if mkt in earliest_dep:
            earliest_dep[mkt] = min(earliest_dep[mkt], deptime)
            latest_dep[mkt] = max(latest_dep[mkt], deptime)
            earliest_arr[mkt] = min(earliest_arr[mkt], arrtime)
            latest_arr[mkt] = max(latest_arr[mkt], arrtime)
        else:
            earliest_dep[mkt] = deptime
            latest_dep[mkt] = deptime
            earliest_arr[mkt] = arrtime
            latest_arr[mkt] = arrtime
    df = pd.DataFrame.from_dict(
        dict(
            earliest_dep=earliest_dep,
            latest_dep=latest_dep,
            earliest_arr=earliest_arr,
            latest_arr=latest_arr,
        )
    )
    df["dep_hours_span"] = (df["latest_dep"] - df["earliest_dep"]) / 3600
    df["arr_hours_span"] = (df["latest_arr"] - df["earliest_arr"]) / 3600
    return df


check_market_windows(cfg)
